dockerfile:
FROM python:3.9-slim

# Install system dependencies required for O3DE Python development
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    git \
    build-essential \
    libgl1-mesa-dev \
    libx11-dev \
    libxrandr-dev \
    libxinerama-dev \
    libxcursor-dev \
    libxi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /o3de

# Copy requirements file
COPY requirements.txt .

# Install Python dependencies
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy O3DE repository (this would typically be done in a multi-stage build)
# COPY . .

# Set environment variables for O3DE
ENV PYTHONPATH=/o3de

# Default command
CMD ["python", "--version"]
explanation: This configuration provides a minimal Python 3.9 environment for O3DE development. The requirements.txt includes pinned versions for stability, with the O3DE-specific packages using generic version placeholders since exact versions would depend on the specific O3DE release. The Dockerfile includes essential system dependencies needed for graphics and development tools, plus a clean Python environment setup. Note that the actual O3DE source code would typically be handled in a multi-stage build or volume mount in a real development scenario.
